records.title: Transit Searches for Habitable-Zone Exoplanets with Artificial Intelligence
records.abstract: Searching for Earth-sized planets in stellar habitable zones ultimately means finding a small number of very shallow, widely separated transits in noisy light curves. Around Sun-like stars, habitable-zone planets generally have long orbital periods, so a finite observing baseline may record only a few transits. At the same time, intrinsic stellar variability, instrumental systematics, and data gaps can obscure these weak events or produce transit-like brightness changes. This review examines recent progress in AI-assisted light-curve preprocessing, weak-signal searches, candidate vetting, and…
